source.what: Rows that PostgreSQL 18.6 returned for the PostgreSQL bytes of each SQLite B2 cell that postgres_replay_v1.json does not hold (Phase78 R1, PL.47): every single-file T2 cell of tests/test_sql_sqlite_native.py (its _T2_CELLS), emitted by emit_postgres_sql, then every project cell of its _PROJECT_CELLS that the PostgreSQL project pipeline emits (literal policy preserve), over the PostgreSQL contract below; each program with sqlite.table(" swapped for postgres.table(". Premise controls and -nocase variants are SQLite-only premises; postgres_refused lists the cells that pipeline refuses.
source.campaign: Preregistration v2.3 with delta r2, attempt 1 of the R1 campaign, PASS exit 0; the campaign ended with this run. Outer wall time 14.68 s (charged 15 s of the campaign's two hours, D78.11). The 105 entries of postgres_replay_v1.json were reused, not replayed (D78.10).
source.container: --pull=never --network none, under PostgreSQL slot lock 2 of 3, removed by its label after the run

regeneration: No command regenerates this file (golden-fixture policy). The replay driver wrote records.jsonl and result.json; each entry here copies, in manifest order, its record's sql_sha256, sent, columns, type_oids and rows verbatim (a value is [type, text] as the replay driver wrote it: repr for int, float, str and bool; null is NULL; sent is each argument's type OID, format and bytes in hex as psycopg sent them), the manifest's parameters (physical type and value) and AVG_ORDER candidates, and the judge's divergences; fixtures copy the manifest's tables and PostgreSQL contracts. When an entry's PostgreSQL bytes, arguments, fixture rows, contract, prewritten oracle or carriers change, or a refused cell starts to emit, test_each_r1_postgres_replay_binds_the_bytes_it_ran in tests/test_sql_sqlite_native.py fails. Then the manifest is generated again from the tree, the changed or new entries run under a reviewed preregistration delta and D78.08's conditions, and a reviewed edit replaces only those entries and the source block; every unchanged entry keeps its saved rows (docs/development.md, SQLite target validation).
not_verified: HAVING with Int, Text and Float query parameters: the only such cell, project-t2-having-parameters, also compares a Bool parameter, which PostgreSQL project mode refuses.
A Bool query parameter echoed in select or read bare in where: the cells hold it only beside refused Bool comparisons.
Binding a pg_bool argument at all: the bound arguments are pg_int8, pg_text and pg_float8 only.
The Bool-name cells (_BOOL_NAME_CELLS) in either mode.
The one-sided sum overflow (sum-over, sum-under): only the in-range bounds sum-up and sum-down ran; PostgreSQL's SQLSTATE 22003 there stays inferred.
